facts.value: Students benefit from the broad expertise in biology and the outstanding computer science resources at Goethe University, as well as the many research institutes and industrial hubs in Frankfurt and the surrounding area.

Literature analysis aims to employ computational and statistical linguistics to mine this growing library of text resources. Examples include abbreviation recognition, named-entity recognition, and protein-protein interaction identification.

Computational technologies are used to automate the processing, quantification, and analysis of large amounts of high-information-content biomedical imagery. Image analysis is important for diagnostics and research.
Computational techniques are used to analyse high-throughput, low-measurement single cell data, finding populations of cells relevant to a particular disease state or experimental condition.
Biological ontologies are directed acyclic graphs of controlled vocabularies, creating categories for biological concepts so they can be easily analyzed with computers.
Databases are essential for bioinformatics research and applications, containing empirical and predicted data for DNA and protein sequences, molecular structures, phenotypes, and biodiversity.
Commonly used databases include Genbank, UniProt, Protein Data Bank (PDB), InterPro, Pfam, and Metabolic Pathway Databases (KEGG, BioCyc).
Software tools for bioinformatics include command-line tools, graphical programs, and web-services, created by bioinformatics companies or public institutions.
Open-source bioinformatics software includes Bioconductor, BioPerl, Biopython, BioJava, BioJS, BioRuby, Bioclipse, EMBOSS, and others.
Bioinformatics workflow management systems provide an easy-to-use environment for scientists to create, execute, and share workflows, and track results.

The BioCompute paradigm aims to create digital 'lab notebooks' for reproducibility, replication, review, and reuse of bioinformatics protocols, allowing for continuity and idea exchange in research groups.

Notable bioinformatics conferences include European Conference on Computational Biology (ECCB), Intelligent Systems for Molecular Biology (ISMB), Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing (PSB), and Research in Computational Molecular Biology (RECOMB).
